text: Professional OverviewNew Energy and Power Engineering focuses on the "clean, low-carbon, efficient and sustainable" principles, researching the development theories of various new energy sources such as solar energy, wind energy, water energy, biomass energy, geothermal energy, hydrogen energy, and nuclear energy (advanced nuclear energy technologies within the scope of new energy). It also studies the application technologies of energy in conversion (such as light-to-heat conversion, electromechanical conversion), storage (such as lithium batteries, hydrogen energy storage), and power systems (such as power for new energy vehicles, distributed energy systems). It is both an extension of traditional power engineering and a key discipline for promoting the transformation of the energy structure.Training ObjectivesThe program aims to cultivate interdisciplinary talents with a solid foundation in energy science (such as thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics), proficient in professional skills such as new energy power generation technology, energy storage technology, and power system design and optimization, and capable of engaging in technical research, engineering design, system operation and management in fields such as new energy development, power systems, automotive engineering, and energy conservation and environmental protection. Students are required to possess both theoretical analysis and technical application abilities, and to focus on solving efficiency improvement and environmental protection issues in energy utilization.
